scope: Named validate constraints in the pinned SysML and KerML metamodels only.
limitations: Source mentions include comments and private tests; they are navigation aids, not implementation or execution proof.
Registry declarations do not certify behavior. Missing names do not prove missing implementations.
Only direct assessment source edges are listed. Each applies to its stated obligation, not necessarily the whole rule.
Mapped tests are not execution results. Use the separately verified requirements execution report.
Derivations, semantic check constraints, operations, grammar, prose, libraries and interchange remain separate review queues.

assessments.obligation: AcceptActionUsage has at least two owned input parameters: its inout payload precedes its input receiver, including when via is omitted.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-022 covers written and omitted receivers, payload values, directed body members, state subactions and transition triggers. Raw graph tests check ownership, direction, parameter ordering and omitted-receiver isImplied provenance. A registered private test mutates receivers to out/inout and excludes inherited input from the owned count. Public ordinary accepts expose ordered parameters; transition accepter records remain navigation stubs with membersAvailable false. Default receiver value/binding, full trigger receiver binding, all implicit relationships, arbitrary inconsistent graphs and execution remain open.

assessments.obligation: Reject non-private root imports while accepting private imports.
assessments.limits: The Rust foundation test additionally exhausts 32 dialect/import-kind/visibility/nesting partitions. Public abstract-syntax import ownership and visibility queries remain unavailable.

assessments.obligation: Check collisions between comparable member metaclasses, including aliases versus inherited members and short/long-name collisions.
assessments.limits: Imported-membership collisions and specialized membership overrides are not exhaustively covered; this is bounded evidence, not qualification of the whole rule.

assessments.obligation: A parallel StateDefinition has no directly owned ActionUsage with an incoming or outgoing TransitionUsage, regardless of the transition owner.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-019 checks source and target independently across the explicit model, including imported cross-file endpoints, and reports the owning state once. Plain Successions, inherited actions, grandchildren and nonowning aliases do not count as directly owned actions. PerformActionUsage retains its own identity instead of following its ReferenceSubsetting. State subaction memberships contribute their owned actions. Missing first/middle/final chain links and ambiguous references cannot establish an endpoint, but a known opposite endpoint remains a violation witness. The endpoint preflight uses shared derived source/target queries, checks written relationship resolution and explicit index bounds, and limits each endpoint proof to the existing work allowance. STATE-003 through STATE-005 and STATE-007 exercise these boundaries; private tests also retain repeated-query and index/work refusal behavior. The target-end selection follows the current lowering representation with an implicit source end. Full transition construction, inherited/implicit connector ends, all endpoint derivations, triggers/guards/effects, arbitrary raw graph consistency and complete state semantics remain unqualified. No public state-slot or membership-metaclass API is added.

assessments.obligation: A StateDefinition has at most one owned StateSubactionMembership of each kind; duplicate findings identify the pinned rule.
assessments.limits: Separate entry/do/exit duplicates, anonymous/named actions, valid peers and locally repeated inherited kinds are exercised. KERNEL-017 corrects the public rule codes while preserving legacy diagnostic message text. Ownership validity, all action-body alternatives, membership kind exposure, derived state action properties and parallel-state transition rules remain unqualified.

assessments.obligation: A StateSubactionMembership must be owned by a StateDefinition or StateUsage, including subclasses.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-021 retains structural findings for invalid part/action bodies and adds the named semantic owner constraint. Definitions, usages and ExhibitStateUsage are positive peers; private graph mutations exercise all three subaction kinds. Full raw graph consistency, implicit membership construction and complete state semantics remain open.

assessments.obligation: An effect TransitionFeatureMembership must own an ActionUsage.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-021 checks the explicit membership owner and actual member metaclass. The public PerformActionUsage effect is admitted; private mutation to ReferenceUsage is rejected without following its referent. The public textual grammar supplies valid typed memberships; malformed-kind/owner negative evidence is the registered private dependency suite. Arbitrary inconsistent raw ownership graphs, semantic metadata construction, guard Boolean/multiplicity qualification and complete transition-feature derivations remain open.

assessments.obligation: A TransitionFeatureMembership must belong to a TransitionUsage.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-021 checks the explicit membership owner and actual member metaclass. Private mutation of the transition owner to an ActionUsage rejects both trigger and effect memberships. The public textual grammar supplies valid typed memberships; malformed-kind/owner negative evidence is the registered private dependency suite. Arbitrary inconsistent raw ownership graphs, semantic metadata construction, guard Boolean/multiplicity qualification and complete transition-feature derivations remain open.

assessments.obligation: A trigger TransitionFeatureMembership must own an AcceptActionUsage.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-021 checks the explicit membership owner and actual member metaclass. Private mutation to PerformActionUsage is rejected even though that target remains an ActionUsage. The public textual grammar supplies valid typed memberships; malformed-kind/owner negative evidence is the registered private dependency suite. Arbitrary inconsistent raw ownership graphs, semantic metadata construction, guard Boolean/multiplicity qualification and complete transition-feature derivations remain open.

assessments.obligation: A transition owns at least one input; a triggered transition owns at least two, with the textual source slot preceding its payload.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-021 fixes the missing first EmptyParameterMember. Raw canonical and legacy graphs cover explicit, target shorthand, guarded action succession and directed body forms; the public full-library query preserves the effective transitionLinkSource and payload identities. The validator selects shared derived inputs owned by the transition, excluding inherited and output-only features while admitting inout. Private mutations verify deficient untriggered/triggered inputs. Guarded/default action-succession grammar omits the empty slot although the common metamodel rule requires it; the builder constructs that input as implied. The AST retains grammar, contextual or semantic parameter origin; conditional targets use their state/action owner context, including state subtypes. Raw-graph tests verify provenance before and after formatting. Guarded entry transitions use the semantic-only slot even in a state body; repeated guards and intervening target successions preserve that entry context until an ordinary member resets it. Normalized external JSON lifting and complete implied-relationship interchange remain unqualified. This is not qualification of every implicit binding, payload chain, inherited feature interaction, raw-payload import/lift round trip or complete transition semantics.

assessments.obligation: A resolved written transition succession target has an ActionUsage as its Feature.featureTarget; incomplete targets do not establish a wrong-kind diagnostic.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-019 prevents an incomplete target chain from becoming a known non-action target. A general ReferenceUsage that references an action is still not an ActionUsage; a PerformActionUsage retains its own ActionUsage identity. The check uses the first owned Succession and its second owned end, matching the shared transition target query and current textual lowering. This is bounded target-kind validation, not qualification of the complete validateTransitionUsageSuccession obligation: missing-succession cases, every target of nonbinary/raw connector forms, implied ends and all malformed ownership configurations remain open. Resolution diagnostics remain independently visible.

assessments.obligation: A triggered transition with a known non-StateUsage source is invalid; the source is its first qualifying ActionUsage feature target, not an unrelated membership or a performed action referent.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-020 uses the shared triggerAction derivation and the KERNEL-019 checked source proof. STATE-008 includes a state source with an unrelated alias, a chained state source, direct and chained PerformActionUsage sources referencing states, ordinary action sources, absent and broken sources, and an untriggered action source. A missing source cannot establish the non-StateUsage antecedent; valid state identity is not replaced by an unrelated membership. Private coverage retains meaningful ambiguous endpoint candidates. Complete transition construction, raw/nonbinary graph forms, all trigger payloads, transition feature validation, guard/effect semantics and execution remain unqualified.

assessments.obligation: A ViewDefinition has at most one ViewRenderingMembership among its owned and inherited feature memberships.
assessments.limits: KERNEL-018 includes inherited ViewRenderingMemberships after shared visibility, membership identity and actual/transitive redefinition reduction. VIEW-001–006 exercise owned/inherited duplicates on definitions and usages, same-name renderings without redefinition, diamonds, private/protected memberships, public re-export, root imports and ordinary renderings, missing bases/redefinitions/imports, cycles and complete peers. Two owned memberships remain a definite violation despite incomplete heritage. The dependency preflight follows base and import namespaces, owned features and explicit redefinition targets; it conservatively audits private import dependencies because import-all may admit them. Syntax recovery in a contributing user document prevents an inherited-count verdict. General metadata-driven membership construction, all filter/import-all interactions, malformed raw graph injection and full view semantics remain unqualified. An absent diagnostic is not a validity certificate. Native/WASM mixed-corpus and both file orders retain earlier assertions; the public snapshot shape is unchanged.
